question: Why are North rentals down on last year since May?

# North Rentals vs Last Year Since May

**Your observation is correct.** North has been below last year since May, though the gap starts the week of 11 May, not the week of 4 May. I can't tell you why from this data. The new price list is the clearest candidate, but the data doesn't prove it caused the drop.

## What the data shows

Same fiscal weeks compared (fiscal week 1 = 2026-04-06 vs 2025-04-07):

| Period | This year | Last year | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weeks 1–4 (6 Apr – 3 May) | 18,879 | 18,786 | +93 (+0.5%) |
| Weeks 5–12 (4 May – 28 Jun) | 38,149 | 41,808 | −3,659 (−8.8%) |

Weekly detail from May:

| Week | This year | Last year | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 May | 4,686 | 4,676 | +0.2% |
| 11 May | 4,494 | 5,193 | −13.5% |
| 18 May | 4,933 | 5,030 | −1.9% |
| 25 May | 4,642 | 5,185 | −10.5% |
| 1 Jun | 4,931 | 5,069 | −2.7% |
| 8 Jun | 4,638 | 5,532 | −16.2% |
| 15 Jun | 4,787 | 5,672 | −15.6% |
| 22 Jun | 5,038 | 5,451 | −7.6% |

**All three depots are down** in weeks 5–12:
- D01 Hollin Cross: −1,430 (−8.4%)
- D02 Petherby: −863 (−7.3%)
- D03 Scarrow Bridge: −1,366 (−10.5%)

**This year hasn't fallen.** North averaged about 4,720 days a week in April and about 4,770 from May onward. The gap exists because last year rose from about 4,700 to about 5,230 over the same period, and this year didn't. With only one prior year, I can't say whether last year's rise was normal seasonality or unusual.

**It isn't a data gap.** No North weekly files are missing for either period.

## What lines up with the timing

- **New North list prices took effect on 4 May 2026** (price list record and D01 staff note). The year-on-year gap appears from the following week.
- **D02 Petherby note, 19 May:** "Several regulars grumbling about the new prices. Two said they would shop around." This is a direct customer reaction, but it is anecdotal and from one depot.

The other notes don't apply to the North. The Tidesend walkout is in the South, and the Carrick Stowe closure is in the West.

## What I can't determine from this data

- **How big the price change was** or how it compares to last year's pricing.
- **Which equipment categories** lost the most on-rent days, so I can't check whether the drop is concentrated in repriced categories.
- **Whether other factors played a part**, such as fleet availability, local demand, competitor activity, weather, or one-off large hires last year. The data doesn't cover these.
- **Whether other regions show the same pattern.** The South repriced on 6 April and would be a useful comparison, but no South or West rental data was provided.

**To test the price explanation,** the most useful next steps would be:
- Break down North on-rent days by category for this year and last.
- Pull the South's weekly figures and see whether a similar gap opened after its April price change.
